transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Thank you. Well, what brings me in today is just this constant restless feeling I've been having. It’s like I’m wound too tight and I just can’t fully settle down. It happens even when I’m supposed to be completely calm—like if I'm sitting through a long planning meeting for work, or even during my own time when I'm painting or trying to do yoga. I just can't seem to shake it.
Is this restless feeling you're describing accompanied by any recurring thoughts or worries?

No, not really. It's not like I'm sitting there worrying about something specific or having anxious thoughts running through my head. It's just a physical feeling, like my body needs to be moving, even when my mind is perfectly fine.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or having an urge to move parts of your body when you're feeling this restlessness?

Yes, definitely. Like, when I'm on calls with suppliers, my foot is usually bouncing under the desk. And I'm... well, I'll be clicking a pen or twisting my ring around. I actually do it so much that I often have to put myself on mute so they don't hear the pen clicking, or I have to consciously move my hands out of view of the camera. It's just a constant urge to be doing something with my hands or feet.
Does this restless feeling happen in every situation, or are there specific times or places where it's more or less pronounced?

Well, I'm not really sure if there's a specific pattern to it. It just kind of happens. I mean, I notice it more when I'm supposed to be sitting still, like I mentioned with the meetings or yoga, but I wouldn't say it goes away completely at other times. It's just... always kind of there in the background, I guess. I haven't really tracked if it's worse in certain places.
Do you notice this restless feeling being worse when you're feeling stressed, angry, or upset?

Um, no, not really. I haven't noticed it being tied to my mood like that. I mean, work can definitely be stressful sometimes, dealing with shipments and all that, but the restlessness doesn't really seem to spike just because I'm stressed or upset. 

Even on a perfectly good, calm day, I'll still be bouncing my leg under the desk or messing with my ring. It just seems pretty separate from how I'm feeling emotionally.
Do you ever feel like you have to perform specific rituals or behaviors to relieve the restlessness or to feel right?

No, I don't think so. I don't have any specific rituals or anything like that. It's just a general need to move, not a routine I have to follow to feel okay. I just move my hands or feet because they feel restless, not because I have to do it a certain way.
Do you notice the restlessness being worse at certain times of the day?

Not really, no. I haven't noticed it being tied to the morning or evening or anything like that. It's pretty consistent throughout the whole day. Like I said before, it's just always kind of there in the background, no matter what time it is.
Has this restlessness affected your relationships or daily activities in any way?

Yeah, it has. At work, um, it's led to some mistakes with my purchase orders, so I've had to go back and correct them. Because of that, my planning coordinator has actually had to start doing extra reviews of my work. And then at home... well, family dinners can get a little tense. Everyone feels like I'm talking over them. So, yeah, it definitely impacts my day-to-day.
Have you noticed any difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep due to this restless feeling?

No, I haven't really noticed any issues with that. I mean, once I'm in bed and ready to sleep, I usually fall asleep just fine. The restlessness doesn't seem to keep me awake or wake me up in the middle of the night.
Do you ever feel any emotional discomfort or anxiety when you're unable to move or engage in the fidgeting behaviors?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I don't really get anxious or upset if I can't move around. It's more just... a physical urge to do it. But if I'm stuck in a long vendor meeting or something and absolutely have to keep still, I don't feel emotionally uncomfortable. It's not an anxiety thing for me.
Do you have any thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, even when you try to focus on something else?

No, not really. I don't get stuck on thoughts like that. Um, my mind might jump around a bit to different things I need to get done for work, but I don't have the same thought just repeating over and over in my head.
Do you feel like there's anything in particular that you're trying to achieve or avoid by fidgeting or moving around?

No, I don't think there's a specific goal or anything. I'm not trying to avoid anything or make something happen. It's just... I just do it. It's not really a conscious choice where I'm thinking, "I need to tap my foot so I can achieve this." It just happens.
Do you feel like your fidgeting or moving around is related to any specific thoughts or mental images?

No, not at all. It's really not connected to anything going on in my head. Like I said, it's just a physical thing. I'm not picturing anything or thinking about anything specific when I do it. I just... fidget.
How long have you been experiencing this restless feeling?

Well, I'd say it's been noticeably harder to manage for about two years and two months now. That's right around the time when, um, some conflicts with my in-laws really started taking over more of our evenings. So, yeah, it's been since then.
Have you ever had difficulty sustaining focus on tasks or activities, even when you're interested in them?

No, I haven't really had that problem. If I'm interested in something, or even just doing my regular work, I can stay focused on it just fine. My issue is more about the physical restlessness, not really my attention span.
Did you experience similar feelings of restlessness or difficulty sitting still as a child?

Yes, I actually did. Um, I remember back in elementary school, my parents would get notes sent home from my teachers. It was usually because I kept popping out of my seat during class. I also had a habit of talking over my classmates, or... I'd rush to blurt out an answer before the teacher even finished asking the question. So, yeah, that difficulty sitting still has been around for a long time.
